sentences.text: Eocaiman is an extinct genus of South American alligatorid, a member of the order Crocodilia within the class Sauropsida. As a reptile in the phylum Chordata and kingdom Animalia, it represents a significant lineage of ancient crocodilians.
Taxonomically, the genus belongs to the family Alligatoridae and the subfamily Caimaninae, placing it among the ancestors of modern caimans.
The genus was named by Simpson in 1933, with the holotype AMNH 3158 found in Argentina and identified as Eocaiman cavernensis.
A second species, Eocaiman palaeocenicus, was discovered in the Salamanca Formation in Argentina and named by Bona in 2007.
The third known species, Eocaiman itaboraiensis, was identified in São José de Itabora, Brazil, by Pinheiro in 2013.
Scientists have also found an undescribed species at the La Venta site in Colombia.
There are currently seven recorded fossil occurrences of Eocaiman, though the genus is divided into four species, some of which are considered doubtful.
The species Notocaiman stromeri was once considered a synonym of Eocaiman but is no longer classified as such.

Species of Eocaiman lived from the Early Paleocene to the Miocene in what is now Argentina, Brazil, and Colombia. Their time range spans from the Danian to the Tortonian, covering approximately 66 to 11 million years ago.

While the genus spans the Paleocene and Miocene, specific dating varies by species: Eocaiman cavernensis dates to the Eocene, Eocaiman palaeocenicus to the Paleocene, and Eocaiman itaboraiensis to both the Paleocene and Eocene.
